title: Sovereign Egress Orchestrator + Permitlist Enforcement
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement a Sovereign Egress Orchestrator that enforces tenant-scoped permitlists/denylist rules for EU-only and other residency-constrained customers. The orchestrator will be a programmable policy layer that evaluates request metadata (tenant, consent headers, contract residency, region preference, SLA tier) and selects an allowed outbound egress target or a safe fallback. This work extends existing routing guards to support per-tenant dynamic permitlists, precedence rules, emergency passthrough, and comprehensive audit logging.
acceptance_criteria: Policy engine can resolve tenant residency and return an egress target (regional-hosted / dedicated-pool / private-deployment) within 5ms median for cached decisions
Support declarative tenant permitlist and denylist entries via Console and API; updates reflected in runtime within 30s
Fallback model variant selection when primary target is unavailable: same-major-architecture variant in-residency -> cross-region encrypted-only path with audit and customer opt-in
Audit logs created for every policy decision with tenant_id, resolved_rule, decision_reason, selected_target, and gRPC request_id
Integration tests covering permitlist precedence (deny > allow per explicit tenant exceptions) and emergency passthrough with RBAC gating
tasks: Write policy schema and precedence matrix (permitlist, denylist, resident-only flag, emergency_passthrough)
Implement runtime cache for resolved tenant policies with TTL and invalidation hook from Console updates
Add HTTP middleware to call orchestrator and annotate request context with chosen route and fallback metadata
Expose CRUD API for tenant-level permitlists in control plane and wire to Console UI
Instrument trace spans and add audit event pipeline (Kafka topic + retention)
Add unit + integration tests; e2e test against a simulated EU and non-EU region cluster
Prepare migration script for existing tenant rules and docs for Customer Success
design_notes: Precedence: explicit denylist entries should always override allowlist; tenant-level exceptions take priority over org-level defaults
Policy evaluation is deterministic and must be idempotent: include tie-breakers for ambiguous residency (contract vs consent header)
Caching: keep small in-memory LRU cache in router with 60s default TTL; changes from Console should publish an invalidation message to runtime via control-plane webhook

Fallbacks: prefer in-region compatible model variant (quantized or smaller context-length) before cross-region egress; cross-region fallback requires customer opt-in unless emergency_passthrough flag is set by SRE
Telemetry: record decision_reason codes to enable downstream quality/cost analysis in Console (e.g., ROUTE_OK, FALLBACK_IN_REGION, FALLBACK_CROSS_REGION, DENY_BLOCK)
Security: every cross-region egress must be encrypted and recorded; private deployments honor local KMS and never route externally
implementation_notes: New package: infra/egress-orchestrator with a pluggable policy evaluator (written in Go)
Leverage existing Geo Policy Decision Service (ENG-52340) interfaces but add tenant-scoped delta rules and faster read path
Control plane API: POST /v1/tenants/{id}/permitlist with optimistic concurrency
Middleware will annotate requests with header X-Redwood-Egress-Decision (json-encoded summary) for downstream components
Fallback model mapping table maintained in S3: model_family -> [in-region-variants, cross-region-compatibles] and refreshed hourly
Add feature flag (ff.geo.sovereign_eo) to gate rollout by account tier
testing_plan: Unit tests for policy precedence permutations (tenant deny overrides org allow, consent header overrides default)
Integration test suite that simulates capacity loss in a region and validates fallback selection and audit events
Chaos test: kill dedicated pool node to validate orchestrator routes to next allowed target and triggers alerting
Performance test: ensure policy evaluation < 10ms p95 under 10k qps with cache warm
Security review checklist + pen test on control-plane permitlist API
rollout_plan: Stage 1: Deploy orchestrator in shadow mode for 2 weeks; decisions logged but not enforced (collect decision_reason)
Stage 2: Opt-in enforcement for internal customers and >P2 accounts behind ff.geo.sovereign_eo
Stage 3: Gradual ramp to all EU-residency customers with monitoring on audit-lag and blocked-request errors
Rollback: Toggle ff.geo.sovereign_eo off and resume legacy routing; provide scripted migration to rehydrate caches
